user.title: Pool
user.description: Filtration time, heating time and the energy budget are all calculated from these figures, so nothing has to be entered in hours.

data_description.volume_l: On the box or in the manual. A round pool: diameter (m) x diameter x 0.785 x depth (m) x 1000. Example: Intex 300x200x75 cm filled to 66 cm is 3834 litres.
data_description.depth_m: Actual water depth, not the wall height. Most pools are filled to about 80-90% of the wall.
data_description.surface_m2: Leave blank and it is calculated from volume and depth. Only used for the initial heat-loss guess, which is replaced by a measured value within days.
data_description.target_temp: 28 °C is comfortable for most people. 26 is brisk, 30 is bath-like and noticeably more expensive.
data_description.max_temp: The highest you would ever set. Used to suggest a safe setting for the heat pump's own thermostat.

pump.title: Circulation pump
pump.description: Manufacturers specify pump flow without a filter installed. With a filter in line roughly {derate}% remains, and it drops further as the filter fouls. If you have measured the real flow, tick the box and the figure is used as it is.

data.pump_flow_measured: This is a measured value, not from the datasheet

data_description.pump_flow_m3h: On the pump label or in the manual, often written as 'flow rate' in m³/h or litres per hour. Divide L/h by 1000 for m³/h. Example: a small cartridge pump is around 2-4 m³/h.
data_description.pump_flow_measured: Tick only if you measured it with a flow meter. Otherwise the datasheet figure is reduced by 30% to account for filter resistance.
data_description.pump_power_kw: On the label, in watts. Divide by 1000. Example: 100 W is 0.1 kW.

heat_pump.title: Heat pump
heat_pump.description: Recommendation: set the heat pump's own thermostat to {recommended_setpoint} °C. That keeps full software control below it while giving you a hardware backstop if the software ever fails to switch off. Leave the second COP point blank for a flat curve.

data.hp_cop_low: COP at a second, lower air temperature

data_description.hp_input_kw: The electricity it draws, on the type plate as 'input power' or 'rated input'. Example: 0.58 kW. Do not confuse this with heat output.
data_description.hp_thermal_kw: The heat it delivers, usually the headline figure such as '3 kW'. Normally 4 to 5 times the input power.
data_description.hp_cop_ref_temp: The air temperature the heat output was measured at. Datasheets usually say 26 °C or 24 °C. If unsure, leave at 26.
data_description.hp_cop_low: Optional. The COP at a colder air temperature, if the datasheet lists a second figure. Leave blank for a flat curve.
data_description.hp_cop_low_temp: The air temperature belonging to that second COP, usually 15 °C.
data_description.hp_air_temp_min: Below this the unit refuses to start. Most pool heat pumps stop somewhere between 10 and 15 °C. If unsure, 11 is a safe guess.
data_description.hp_air_temp_max: Rarely relevant in this climate. 43 °C is a typical limit.
data_description.hp_flow_min_m3h: The minimum water flow the unit needs. Often around 2 m³/h. If unsure, leave the default.

entities.title: Required entities
entities.description: The two switches and the pool water temperature. Without these nothing can work.

data_description.pump_switch: The switch or smart plug that powers the circulation pump.
data_description.heat_pump_switch: The switch or smart plug that powers the heat pump.
data_description.water_temp_sensor: The sensor measuring the pool water itself. Take care to pick the right one; it can be changed later under Configure.

optional.title: Optional entities
optional.description: Every field may be left blank; the matching feature is switched off and reported rather than failing. With the figures entered so far, filtration needs about {daily_hours} hours a day, roughly {block_minutes} minutes per block.

data_description.air_temp_sensor: Outdoor air at the installation. Without it the operating envelope cannot be checked and frost protection falls back on the weather entity.
data_description.hp_inlet_sensor: Water going into the heat pump. If your plumbing runs pool → pump → heat pump, the pump outlet sensor is the right choice.
data_description.hp_outlet_sensor: Water coming out of the heat pump. Together with the inlet this gives delta-T and COP.
data_description.flow_sensor: A flow meter in m³/h. Enables flow protection and makes the filtration blocks correct themselves as the filter fouls.
data_description.pump_power_sensor: Power draw of the pump, if your plug measures it.
data_description.hp_power_sensor: Power draw of the heat pump, if your plug measures it. Needed for cost and measured COP.
data_description.price_sensor: A sensor whose state is the price per kWh. Dynamic tariff integrations provide this.
data_description.solar_forecast_sensor: A solar forecast, if you have one.
data_description.weather_entity: Used as a fallback when no outdoor sensor is configured.
data_description.cover_entity: A sensor or switch reporting whether the cover is on. Leave blank if you have none.

swimming.title: Swimming times
swimming.description: One window per weekday covers nearly every household. The second is there for exceptions and may be left blank.

notifications.title: Notifications
notifications.description: Faults repeat with a widening interval until they clear; informational messages fire once. Leave a field blank to use the default target.

data.turnover_factor: Turnover factor (times the pool volume per day)
data.negative_price_basis: Which price counts as below zero
data.stale_warning_seconds: Warn when a reading is older than (seconds)
data.stale_blocking_seconds: Treat a sensor as dead after (seconds)

entities.title: Entities
entities.description: Change which entities the integration uses. Picking the wrong sensor at setup is easy; this is where you correct it. Clearing an optional field switches that feature off again.

hardware.title: Pool and equipment
hardware.description: Correct the figures entered during setup. Filtration duration and heating time are recalculated immediately.
